metadata.requiredArtifacts: Collection-time array of {path, format, allowEmpty}. Paths are fixed by each test case, relative to its run directory and unique across active tests; descriptors do not contain FGO reasons or servant semantics.
metadata.artifactReceipts: Execution-time array of {path, expectedBytes, expectedSha256}, one per required descriptor. Hash the intended final bytes before filesystem writes, never reconstruct an expected checksum from the later file.
metadata.reconciliation: Require one receipt per active requirement, reject missing/extra/duplicate receipts and duplicate normalized paths across tests. Do not silently deduplicate competing declarations via Map last-write-wins.
metadata.activation: Require artifacts for passed or failed tests; filtered-out tests do not acquire obligations. Preserve existing skip/todo/timeout/signal/reporter-failure gates. A collection/beforeAll failure remains nonzero even when no test body ran; do not claim a complete audit was produced.
metadata.reportMissing: Missing/invalid vitest.json remains reporter/test failure under existing outcome precedence. With a report present, a required descriptor lacking a receipt is artifact_failure even if the child reported success.
metadata.metadataMissing: A typed test-definition helper must install the collection-time contract and the writer must reject an absent contract. A focused real-reporter contract must assert that metadata survives. A generic runner cannot infer a removed source declaration from a file name or domain reason.

payload.contents: Preserve the entire supplied gate, all failures in original order, all supplied observations and existing selected candidate traces. Keep production and fixture artifacts distinct by origin and path. No console truncation, grouping or sampling in the artifact.
payload.completeness: Complete means all data produced by the existing invocation. It is not proof of a fresh control identity population, alternate execution coverage or a production stale-mutation consumer.
payload.serialization: The implementation used the proposed artifact-only versioned envelope with undefinedPaths. A focused existing producer run disproved the proposal as complete: calculator[0].portable.execution.effectiveContributions.effectivePresentationGroupIds is a Set, and the serializer currently rejects non-plain objects. Do not omit or coerce this generated trace. An artifact-only Set representation is a proposed plan revision, not implemented or verified.
payload.unsupportedTransportValues: The current implementation rejects cycles, functions, symbols, bigint, non-finite numbers, sparse arrays and non-plain objects. This remains fail-closed but is insufficient for the observed Set in the existing Battle Point producer. Keep rejection for unhandled shapes; do not stringify or drop them. Any newly supported artifact representation must remain outside canonical input and digest calculations.
payload.domainValidation: Application-side gate validation requires the existing typed reason/identity and a firstDifference object with identity/path/expected/actual presence for a failed gate. Undefined expected/actual values are legal and preserved; missing firstDifference is not. Empty path may mean a root difference. Preserve each existing union shape, including top-level parity mismatch with an empty subordinate failures array.
payload.snapshotVsGate: Existing scenario mutation/rollback observation snapshots with firstDifference:null are snapshots, not failed gates. Transport migration must not reinterpret these as a new stale-mutation ratchet.
payload.malformedGate: Serialize the available payload before raising its diagnostic-contract error, so missing reason/identity/firstDifference is not repaired or discarded. This artifact is malformed-domain evidence, not a valid/passing gate.
payload.digest: Preserve the producer source/digest and typed mismatch unchanged. Artifact byte SHA-256 is transport integrity only; no new canonical digest or TSK-06.5 expected-value update.

preferredDesign.canonicalExpectation: Keep hpPreparationCanonicalFor/getSkillsForActorForm as canonical source generators. Unit52 owns one immutable pre-evaluation declaration/choice ledger and scope contract; no activation/eligibility/native-success filter. Static preflight is a declaration join, not success evidence. Do not store full irrelevant executions or recanonicalize identical requests repeatedly solely to populate separate lists.
preferredDesign.typedEvidence: Create focused selectedAlly evidence/proof module in calculation-application, with explicit fields for command/form/source occurrence/operation/value cells, HP/modifier/receipt values and native/reducer/selected reader/NP/input/result links. Represent boundary dispositions exhaustively; malformed/missing evidence fails the audit rather than empty-list/value fallback. Product invalid/unsupported/native classification stays unchanged.
preferredDesign.liveOwnership: Separate raw reference anchors from canonical value proof and persisted codec. Keep necessary HP leaf owner anchors so same-valued reader/NP copies fail. Capture remains an observer immediately after original apply; no arithmetic, writer replay, inferred downstream or whole state graph identity requirement.
preferredDesign.graphComparison: Normalize accepted proof values once per audit invocation and compare shared graph pairs without repeated tree expansion. Expected authority snapshot remains immutable. Memoization must be local to one synchronous gate invocation, because committed denial fixtures mutate/restore original sources between invocations; global WeakMap caches would return stale proofs. Preserve typed reason/checkPath and canonical first difference; repeated failing paths must remain addressable even if equal subgraphs are skipped. Freeze complete actual denial values during the gate call, before the fixture restores its mutable source. Do not retain raw live values for lazy later diagnostic construction. Cache by object plus semantic-view kind if extraction uses different views; a single cross-view object cache can suppress fields.
preferredDesign.restoration: Artifact transport owns one complete encode/write/receipt/read/decode/restoration operation before semantic assertions. Prefer graph-aware restoration equality under the exact current accepted value contract (undefined versus missing, ordered Set/Map, null-prototype objects, keys/prototypes, cycle/invalid values); do not replace independent payload equality solely with re-encode equality, because encoder/decoder could share an error. Repeated per-task restoration work may only be removed when the remaining single disk roundtrip proves the same full payload and all declarations/receipts remain.
preferredDesign.resultAndArtifact: Use one shared complete value graph in checks/diagnostic, with full expected/actual values reachable by typed proof addresses. All successful checks and all failures remain reconstructible; no sampling, lazy failure-only payload, first-difference-only artifact, losing owner proof or numerical fallback. Preserve current artifact envelope/digest versions unless measured design necessity justifies a separately explicit contract migration. No codec replacement just for speculative speed. A shared immutable proof node table is built at gate time, not inferred later from successful results. Persist ownership-check outcomes separately because content interning deliberately merges equal values and cannot reconstruct runtime reference identity.
preferredDesign.productionInventory: Within data-pipeline, share strict parsed master/allEffects/operation-family inventory across the direct execution-semantics assertions. Application HP inventory owns its own canonical cell inventory and executes all cells through original HP owner. Give readiness/read/parse/compile explicit measured lifecycle assertions and error propagation; retain existing timeout/threshold coverage, account for setup work rather than move it outside budget. Do not implement a cross-worker mutable singleton, alternate cache file, alternate credentials or partial-schema parser. File/process isolation prevents claiming one package-wide parse merely from an imported Promise helper. First share within the directly affected suite/model; any cross-file consolidation needs explicit suite coverage/lifecycle ownership and measured counters, without weakening isolation or removing cases.
